name: Toyota Sienna
engine: 2.5L Atkinson-cycle I4 hybrid (A25A-FXS) paired with electric motors, 245 hp combined
torque: 176 lb-ft (engine); the hybrid system's electric assist fills in low-end torque
drivetrain: FWD or electronic AWD (a separate rear electric motor drives the rear axle)
reliability: 8/10 — the fourth-gen Sienna made a bold move to hybrid-only power, and it pairs Toyota's very proven hybrid system with minivan practicality to deliver around 36 mpg, which is transformative for a vehicle this size. The powertrain is dependable and the fuel savings are real. The main complaints are that the four-cylinder can sound strained and buzzy under hard acceleration (there is no V6 anymore), and some owners wanted more outright passing punch. As a durable, efficient family hauler, it is hard to beat.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate · Maintenance ~$500/yr · Excellent fuel economy for a minivan (~35 mpg real-world) makes it cheap to run · Strong resale — efficient three-row Toyotas hold value well
popular_mods: All-weather floor liners and a full-length cargo liner — non-negotiable for family and road-trip duty
Sunshades, seat-back organizers, and a trash/console setup for kid duty
Roof crossbars plus a cargo box for luggage on trips
A second set of winter tires for the AWD in cold climates
Honest take: the Sienna is about space and efficiency, not speed — money is best spent on protection, tires, and family-friendly accessories

generations.3rd Gen XL30 (2011–2020 US): The V6, available-AWD Sienna — 3.5L V6 with a 6- then 8-speed automatic, and the only minivan of its era offered with all-wheel drive. Roomy and durable.
generations.4th Gen XL40 (2021–present US): A dramatic redesign that went hybrid-only — a 245 hp four-cylinder hybrid, e-CVT, available electronic AWD, and around 36 mpg. Clever storage (Super Long Slide second row) and available onboard amenities.
generations.Note: Because the fourth gen is hybrid-only, there is no V6 option after 2020 — the trade for the big jump in fuel economy.

common_issues: The 2.5L four sounds strained and buzzy under hard acceleration — the character trade for hybrid efficiency, not a fault
Some owners want more passing power than the hybrid four delivers when fully loaded
Early infotainment quirks and occasional software updates on the first (2021) model year
Brake feel from the regenerative system takes some getting used to
Confirm any open recalls by VIN, as with any recent vehicle
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the 0W-16 synthetic oil on the Maintenance Minder
Keep the traction-battery cooling intake (in the cabin) clear of debris, and keep the 12V battery healthy
Service brake fluid on schedule; regen means pads last a long time but fluid still needs changing
Rotate tires and budget for them given the vehicle's weight
Have any open recalls confirmed closed by VIN before buying

engine.detail: 2.5L Atkinson-cycle four (A25A-FXS) paired with electric motors for 245 hp combined - hybrid-only, no V6 offered since 2020.
engine.watch: Toyota's hybrid system is very proven and dependable; the four just sounds strained and buzzy under hard acceleration - character, not a fault.

drivetrain.detail: e-CVT (a planetary hybrid transmission) driving the front wheels, with optional AWD via a separate rear electric motor.
drivetrain.watch: Few moving parts and a strong reliability record - largely trouble-free; keep up with routine fluid and coolant service.

brakes.detail: Regenerative braking blended with conventional friction brakes, which recover energy and greatly reduce pad wear.
brakes.watch: Pads last a long time, but some owners report pulsation or grabby feel, and the regen takes getting used to. Service brake fluid on schedule.

electrical.detail: Hybrid traction battery plus a standard 12V battery, and a large touchscreen infotainment system.
electrical.watch: Early 2021 trucks had infotainment quirks fixed by software updates; keep the 12V healthy. The hybrid battery is well-proven and warrantied.

body.detail: Minivan body with dual power sliding doors and clever storage like the Super Long Slide second row.
body.watch: Some owners report water leaks at the sliding-door drains or sunroof. Also confirm the 2021-2025 third-row seatback bolt recall is closed by VIN.
